paper.title: Towards Evidence-Aware Retrieval and Verification for Scientific Fact-Checking
paper.abstract: Scientific fact-checking (SFC) is a critical task that aims to verify scientific claims by finding supporting or refuting evidence from a vast and rapidly growing body of research literature [4]. Unlike general fact-checking, SFC operates in high-stakes domains where incorrect scientific conclusions may influence public policy, medical practice, or future research directions. As scientific publications continue to increase in volume and technical complexity, manually verifying claims becomes infeasible for human experts and fact-checkers. This limitation not only slows knowledge validation but also increases the risk that unverified or misinterpreted findings propagate through academic and public discourse. Consequently, there is an urgent need for automated systems that can assist researchers in ensuring the reliability and integrity of scientific knowledge. A standard fact-checking pipeline typically consists of two main stages: evidence retrieval and claim verification [3]. While the community has made significant progress in claim verification, the retrieval stage is often oversimplified. Most existing studies treat retrieval as a general similarity search, ignoring the specific requirements of the verification process.
